- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5% below peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.  
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–2% per day until convergence to 30-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 1.00 → 0.33 → 1.00), model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day horizon, avoid extreme outliers (> ±5% from 30-day MA) unless sentiment confirms breakout; use sentiment-weighted smoothing to dampen volatility.
